### Subtypes in copied records

Node packages also accept the tested `Nat` Subtype fields in acyclic copied
records and tagged variants. Use `bigint` for each payload and the generated
record fields or variant tags. The package selects the checked Lean constructor
at each input site, so two exports using the same record can normalize its
payload differently. Only the active variant case runs its constructors.
Rejected inputs remain unchanged and later valid calls still work.

Copied outputs project their existing Lean payloads. They do not select or run
an input constructor, and the caller neither supplies nor receives proof fields.
This also applies to a package that only returns these values.

The [installed nominal checks](evidence/nominal-subtype-npm-acceptance-20261011.md)
cover ordinary-source and reviewed packages on Node 22.23.2 with strict
TypeScript, including aliases, mixed `Fin` guards, repeated record fields and
100-bit results. Browser pages, React, workers, other primitive bases and
callback, owned or recursive Subtype combinations need separate acceptance.

Omit the result's `refinement` in an ordinary export contract, or omit `contracts` entirely for a result-only package with unrefined inputs. The shared component compiler no longer requires a result constructor selection. Source-free installed acceptance for these additions is pending across native, npm and PHP-Wasm packages.

edits.previous: Ordinary-source npm packages accept top-level parameters and results over primitive bases, including heap-backed `Nat`, `Int`, `String`, and `ByteArray`. These exports can share a package with arrays, records, recursive values, callbacks, and returned closures. For example, an export may take a checked nonempty string alongside a callback; an empty string rejects before that callback runs. JavaScript and TypeScript use the base type's normal representation. Compiled Lean calls the constructor before the exported function; `none` rejects the host call, while `some` supplies the proof-carrying value. A result is already a Lean subtype and is projected through `.val` at the generated boundary. Rejected inputs release decoded arguments and leave the runtime available for subsequent calls. Field Subtypes have the compiler-stage checks below; Subtype refinements inside callback signatures remain unsupported. [Installed structural checks](../evidence/structural-subtype-promotion-20261011.md) cover both source routes across all seventeen profiles: `Array`, `List`, `Option`, products, `Except`, transparent aliases, mixed `Fin` and one closed `List` specialization. See the [nested constructor-selection syntax](export-decisions.md#select-constructors-inside-containers).
